quote: K. K. But I'm not too sure. Well, let's see what we can do for you.
stewart_read: The customer has just described a flat/split roof with heavy tree shading — a real technical qualification question — and the rep verbally shrugs rather than resolving it or flagging it for the specialist. There is no schema dq_rule that maps cleanly to a shaded-flat-roof scenario, so this is a rep knowledge/follow-through gap rather than a documented protocol violation.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be strategically deferring the technical roof assessment to the specialist's site visit rather than trying to resolve it himself — consistent with setter-scope discipline.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly hand off unresolved technical concerns with a spoken bridge ('the specialist will assess the shading on site') rather than an ambiguous 'let's see what we can do' — the ambiguity means neither the customer nor the closer knows this was flagged.

quote: What company is that? Yeah. What company is that? Iam Solar. I'm
stewart_read: Customer is asking who is calling him again, mid-confusion about a prior door-knock visit — a legitimacy question the rep answers weakly ('Iam Solar') rather than with a clean, specific answer per the schema's honest_specificity pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: This may just be a transcription/audio garble rather than a substantive rep failure, given the surrounding disfluency in the transcript.
coaching_implication: When a customer asks who's calling more than once, the rep should re-anchor legitimacy clearly and specifically rather than a mumbled company name — worth a listen-back to confirm audio vs. actual weak answer.

quote: Somebody come by about that. Yeah. Yeah. And I was thinking pretty serious about getting some of it.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior in-person Ion visit ('somebody come by') and serious intent, a valuable disclosure the rep acknowledges only by pivoting straight back to the bill-photo ask rather than probing what that prior visit covered.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may already know from internal records that this is a repeat touch and is deliberately not re-covering old ground — but nothing in the transcript confirms the rep has that context.
coaching_implication: Flag for lead-type/prior-touchpoint metadata gap: if this is a recycled or re-touched lead, the rep should know and reference what the prior visit covered instead of restarting cold.

quote: Oh, that's well, I'm not sure, but I'm pretty sure it is. Yeah.
stewart_read: Customer gives an explicitly uncertain self-reported credit answer, and the rep accepts it at face value and moves on without any follow-up probing or caveat.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be following standard procedure of accepting stated credit and letting the closer's actual pull be the real gate — which the schema itself flags as an unresolved Kenny policy question.
coaching_implication: This is a clean example of the stated-vs-pulled credit risk the schema calls out — worth surfacing to Kenny as a real instance rather than coaching the rep on wording alone, since the correct procedure isn't yet settled.

quote: I can't do this every day when I have people keep coming over.
stewart_read: Customer signals scheduling fatigue and volume-of-visitors stress right at the point of locking a time — a real barrier to the appointment holding, not just a logistics question.
coaching_implication: The rep pushed through to a booked time without addressing this stated overwhelm directly; the manager should note this as a fragility signal for no-show risk, not treat the booked outcome as clean.

quote: We would love to also meet with your daughter. I know, she might be a little hesitant to meet with us. But if she's available, we can show what we're offering to see if it'll fit your needs.
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies the daughter as a co-title-holder and invites her to the appointment per protocol, but never gets an explicit yes/no on her actual attendance — the invitation is made but not confirmed.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's later line 'she she would prefer Tuesday morning' at 14:05 could be read as implicit confirmation she'll be present, since he's relaying her preference.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to get an explicit confirmation ('will she be on the call/there with you Tuesday?') rather than inferring attendance from a relayed scheduling preference.

quote: Yeah. So, Kevin, so you you you said you you met with Sunrun. Correct? They got you an evaluation already?
stewart_read: Rep names the competitor directly but the follow-up ('They got you an evaluation already?') is answered with a vague non-answer and a stray number ($90/month), and the rep never pins down what equipment, system size, or terms Sunrun actually offered.
coaching_implication: This is exactly the kind of competitive intel the closer needs — coach the rep to ask one more specific question ('what size system, what monthly cost did they quote?') before moving off the topic.
